# Odigos

> Odigos captures the arguments and return values of any function in a live production
> service, in seconds, with no code change and no redeploy, and exports the result as
> OpenTelemetry that you own.

Conventional observability can only answer questions somebody anticipated when the code was
written. Logs, metrics and traces are fixed at deploy time, so when an incident turns on a
value nobody recorded, the only way to get it is to change the code and ship a release.

Odigos decides what to capture at the moment you ask. An AI agent or an engineer can point at
a function, a query or a service that nothing was ever set up to watch, and Odigos attaches
the capture to the running process and returns the values in about a second. That closes the
loop for agents: instead of opening a pull request and waiting for a deploy to get one more
fact, the agent queries production directly and keeps investigating.

It runs out of process in eBPF at under 1% CPU and never loads into the application, so an
Odigos failure cannot take a customer application down. It detects each service's language
automatically and supports Go, Java, Python, .NET, JavaScript, PHP and Ruby, including
compiled binaries that are stripped and statically linked.

Captured data is governed. RBAC controls who may capture what and on which workloads, and PII
masking, attribute deletion and sampling run inside the customer's own cluster before anything
leaves it. Odigos runs alongside Datadog, New Relic, Honeycomb, Grafana and the open source
stack rather than replacing them.
